scope: Case review and live degree-discovery expansion. All404 profiles can be explored;377 have comparable official vectors. The117 guided Top/Other/lifestyle professions retain their existing rules. Profession-function prompts in this research are drafts for later informed exploration, not primary discovery or validated aptitude items.

reviews.title: Market researcher
reviews.conclusion: Valentina’s customer-research clues deserve a focused invitation. There is not enough evidence to promote a Top match.

examples.name: Valentina Salazar
examples.evidence: Resale listings, concise captions and comparing prices connect to investigating customer choices. Three mapped task groups in three domains, but r = 0.547 misses the broad-profile threshold and she has not completed the business branch. Neither current defining-work question was asked.

examples.name: Wyatt Mercer
examples.evidence: The engine lists market research internally despite no mapped task evidence. Both profile-inferred defining answers are unfamiliar. This is a weak generic business bridge, not evidence of an overlooked Top match.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn why different customers choose one product over another, using questions or purchase data rather than only writing the listing?
reviews.action: Follow with analyzing customer evidence and recommending a change. Separate marketing research from selling, copywriting and running a shop.

reviews.title: Exercise physiologist
reviews.conclusion: Darius is a strong exploration lead. The current absence does not justify concluding that nobody is interested.

examples.name: Darius Bell
examples.evidence: Basketball, recovery exercises and coaching younger players justify a comparison with rehabilitation, coaching and clinical exercise work. Five mapped task groups, r = 0.560; full comparison rank 17. It falls outside the chart’s three invitations. Both defining-work questions remain unasked.

examples.name: Finley
examples.evidence: The alternative comparison is rank 14, but homework-club teaching provides much less specific support for clinical exercise testing.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to use exercise-test results to design and adjust an exercise program for someone with a health condition?
reviews.action: Compare exercise physiology with physical therapy, athletic training and fitness coaching. Enjoying sport alone does not establish interest in physiological tests and clinical monitoring.

reviews.title: Nursing Assistants
reviews.conclusion: Offer a concrete care-work comparison before narrowing to one clinical role. A Top match is still unresolved.

examples.name: Jordan
examples.evidence: First-aid practice and repeated team procedures justify explaining bedside care; nursing assistant is comparison rank 7, outside the three invitations. There are two mapped task groups, not confirmed defining-work interest.

examples.name: Sam
examples.evidence: Five mapped care-task groups exist, but choosing another focused clinical role activates roleFocusElsewhere and removes this alternative. Broad care activities do not establish preference for intimate daily care.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to help patients with bathing, dressing and moving safely, while reporting changes to the nurse supervising their care?
reviews.action: Allow several clinical interests. Explain personal care and supervision neutrally; do not infer a preference from being kind or from helping a relative.

reviews.title: Real estate agent
reviews.conclusion: Valentina merits an invitation; Audrey’s unresolved interest should stay unresolved. Neither is a confirmed Top match.

examples.name: Valentina Salazar
examples.evidence: Small resale listings and comparing prices are a bridge to a question, not proof of property representation. Real estate is full comparison rank 8 and both defining questions are unasked.

examples.name: Audrey Whitfield
examples.evidence: Four mapped task groups and r = 0.731 produce an internal related idea at Other rank 8. Her inferred answers are unsure / unfamiliar: browsing fashion and noticing homes do not establish transaction or negotiation interest. Pending items consume some of the six Other slots before removal.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to help a buyer compare properties, understand offers and negotiate a sale, including the paperwork and follow-up?
reviews.action: Contrast representing a client in a property transaction with enjoying houses, interior design, investing or general retail sales.

reviews.title: Social worker (children and families)
reviews.conclusion: Keep the missing-work question. Teaching or general helping does not establish family-service casework.

examples.name: Darius Bell
examples.evidence: The engine reaches provisional support from broad helping evidence, but basketball and recovery practice do not establish interest in family difficulties or coordinating services. Defining questions are unasked.

examples.name: Harper Voss
examples.evidence: Teaching through movement and reading events support education. Both inferred social-work answers are unsure; there is no documented interest in service referrals and case follow-up.

examples.name: Brielle Booker
examples.evidence: A social-work comparison is available at rank 1. The internal related option can also be hidden by the pending-before-cap ordering; visibility would not confirm fit.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to work with a child or family facing difficulties, connect them with services and follow up on a support plan?
reviews.action: Do not require psychotherapy for all social work. Distinguish nonclinical family services from licensed clinical practice.

reviews.title: Mental-health care aide
reviews.conclusion: The current profiles do not establish interest in supporting people in a mental-health care setting.

examples.name: Darius Bell
examples.evidence: Three generic helping groups and a high broad correlation create a pending offer. They do not distinguish psychiatric daily care from sports recovery or other helping work.

examples.name: Sam
examples.evidence: The clinical-role exclusion also applies here. Explain the alternative before interpreting the exclusion as dislike; biology and routine helping alone are insufficient.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to support the daily routines and safety of people receiving mental-health care, under a care team’s direction?
reviews.action: Keep daily supportive care distinct from counseling, nursing and the technician’s treatment-related responsibilities.

reviews.title: Mental-health care technician
reviews.conclusion: No established psychiatric-treatment interest supports a promotion. A separate role explanation is needed.

examples.name: Darius Bell
examples.evidence: The pending offer has three generic task groups. His profile supports recovery and coaching exploration more directly than psychiatric care.

examples.name: Finley
examples.evidence: The full comparison is rank 4, but tutoring interest does not establish interest in observing psychiatric symptoms or implementing a care plan.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to observe changes in a mental-health patient’s condition and carry out treatment activities under a clinical team’s direction?
reviews.action: Explain technician duties separately from aide duties. Never infer comfort with psychiatric treatment from listening to friends.

reviews.title: Fast-food or counter worker
reviews.conclusion: The defining customer-service question is doing useful work. Food preparation and counter service are different interests.

examples.name: Sky
examples.evidence: Sustained cooking supports learning food preparation, but the order/payment question is unsure. The other defining answer is Yes with medium confidence.

examples.name: Wyatt Sloane
examples.evidence: Repeat baking and supply sorting support organized preparation. Taking customer orders is not established; answers are unsure / Yes.

examples.name: Zoe Min Park
examples.evidence: Cake decoration and event baking do not establish liking a customer queue, orders or payment handling.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to take customers’ food orders and payments accurately during a busy service period?
reviews.action: Offer preparation, baking and food science separately. Do not make customer-facing service a default because someone cooks.

reviews.title: Personal Care Aides
reviews.conclusion: Daily personal-care interest needs a direct question even when general health helping is supported.

examples.name: Jordan
examples.evidence: Comparison rank 1 makes this visible for exploration, but first-aid procedures do not establish wanting ongoing personal care.

examples.name: Sam
examples.evidence: Five shared task groups are suppressed by the clinical-role gate. The alternative deserves an explanation, not an automatic upgrade.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to help someone at home with everyday personal care and routines so they can live as independently as possible?
reviews.action: Distinguish nonmedical personal support from licensed nursing tasks; do not use a shorter training route as evidence of interest.

reviews.title: Vocational nurse (LVN)
reviews.conclusion: Broader nursing alternatives deserve comparison. The current absence is not evidence against the occupation.

examples.name: Jordan
examples.evidence: First aid and coordinated procedures make basic nursing a reasonable learning comparison. Full invitation rank 6 leaves it outside the chart’s first three.

examples.name: Sam
examples.evidence: Five mapped groups exist but another focused clinical role suppresses LVN. The stored entry-pay budget would cover Sam’s plan; interest and route still need checking. This illustrates why affordability alone must not assign a profession.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to provide basic nursing care, check patients’ condition and report changes while working under a registered nurse or doctor?
reviews.action: Explain LVN and RN responsibilities and preparation separately; allow interest in both before asking about training preferences.

reviews.title: Mental Health Counselors
reviews.conclusion: The counseling distinction remains necessary. General listening and teaching are not therapy interest.

examples.name: Harper Voss
examples.evidence: Both inferred answers are unsure: listening and teaching do not establish confidential counseling or treatment planning.

examples.name: Darius Bell
examples.evidence: A pending offer from broad helping evidence has unasked defining questions. Recovery exercises are stronger grounds to explore rehabilitation than to infer psychotherapy.

examples.name: Brielle Booker
examples.evidence: Comparison rank 3 exposes counseling as a question. An additional internal related row can be lost to the Other cap; displaying it would not resolve interest.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to use counseling methods to help someone work through emotional difficulties and review progress with them over time?
reviews.action: Separate a wish to support friends from interest in professional therapeutic work and its responsibilities.

reviews.title: Insurance Sales Agents
reviews.conclusion: Keep uncertainty about risk and policy advice. Sales or fashion interest is not enough.

examples.name: Valentina Salazar
examples.evidence: Both inferred defining answers are unfamiliar. Clothes, listing descriptions and sale records do not establish interest in risk, coverage and protection advice.

examples.name: Audrey Whitfield
examples.evidence: Both answers are unfamiliar. Polished presentations and social interests provide no specific policy-sales evidence. The related row is also hidden by the six-slot cap.

examples.name: Jalen Brooks
examples.evidence: Comparison rank 2 makes the idea visible, but neither that rank nor broad correlation establishes a genuine policy interest.

reviews.question: Would you like to learn to compare insurance policies and explain which risks are covered or excluded for a client?
reviews.action: Explain policy advice before re-asking an unfamiliar response; keep quotas, follow-up and sales context separate from financial-analysis interest.

proposals.title: Aerospace Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in aerospace engineering or related field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Design and test flying vehicles and spacecraft
questions: Would you like to learn how to design an aircraft or spacecraft so it can fly or move safely and efficiently?
Would you like to learn to use calculations and prototype tests to improve how an aircraft or spacecraft performs?
proposals.contrast: Which sounds more interesting: designing and testing a flying vehicle, operating it, repairing it, or none of these?
risks: Interest in space news or flying is not enough to establish engineering-design interest. Defense clearance requirements apply to some jobs, not the entire occupation.

proposals.title: Chemical Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in chemical engineering or related field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Turn chemistry into safe, repeatable production processes
questions: Would you like to learn to design a process that turns raw ingredients into useful products such as medicines, fuels, or materials?
Would you like to learn to test how temperature, pressure, and equipment changes can make a production process safer and less wasteful?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather discover what a substance does in a laboratory, design how to make a product at larger scale, both, or neither?
risks: Distinguish process design from chemistry alone or following production instructions; do not require prior plant or calculus experience to express interest.

proposals.title: Computer Hardware Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in computer engineering or related field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Design and test the physical components of computing systems
questions: Would you like to learn to design the physical parts inside a computer or smart device, such as its circuits or processor system?
Would you like to learn to test a new computer component and work out why it fails or does not work well with the software?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather design new computer parts, write applications, help people fix existing computers, or explore more than one?
risks: Gaming, assembling a PC, and troubleshooting can open exploration but do not by themselves establish new-hardware design interest.

proposals.title: Electronics Engineers, Except Computer
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in electrical/electronics engineering or related field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Design electronic circuits and communication/sensing devices
questions: Would you like to learn to design circuits that let devices sense information, communicate, or control what happens?
Would you like to learn to measure signals and test a circuit to make an electronic device work more reliably?
proposals.contrast: Which would you most like to design: electronic sensors and communication devices, power and motors, software, or none?
risks: Avoid double counting a general electrical interest as two independent confirmations. This is a distinct O*NET occupation; show overlap and shared preparation.

proposals.title: Environmental Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in environmental engineering or related engineering field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Design practical systems that prevent or reduce pollution
questions: Would you like to learn to design systems that clean polluted water or reduce waste and air pollution?
Would you like to learn to compare treatment designs using test results, costs, and their effects on people and the environment?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather investigate an environmental problem, design a system to fix it, do outdoor conservation work, or explore several?
risks: Caring about nature is not sufficient to confirm engineering design. Offer a science-to-design bridge rather than require the Engineering field first.

proposals.title: Materials Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in materials engineering or related engineering field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Develop and select materials based on how they behave
questions: Would you like to learn to choose or develop a material that makes a product stronger, lighter, longer-lasting, or easier to recycle?
Would you like to learn to test why a material cracks, wears out, or fails and use the findings to improve it?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather improve what a product is made from, how its moving parts work, how it looks and feels, or none?
risks: Do not turn general art-material use or chemistry curiosity into material-performance interest without a follow-up.

proposals.title: Agricultural Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in agricultural/biological engineering or related engineering field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Engineer equipment and systems for agriculture
questions: Would you like to learn to design equipment or growing systems that help farms use water, energy, or labor more effectively?
Would you like to learn to test a farm’s irrigation, storage, or machinery problem and design a practical improvement?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather grow and care for crops, study the science of crop growth, design farm equipment and systems, or explore several?
risks: Gardening alone is not an engineering confirmation; promising practical farm experience should trigger a design branch. Small occupation: local opportunity requires separate verification.

proposals.title: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in engineering or related field
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Engineer hazards out of equipment and work systems
questions: Would you like to learn to work out how a machine, product, or workplace could injure someone and redesign it to reduce that risk?
Would you like to learn to investigate an accident or test a safety feature and explain what needs to change?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather design safer systems, inspect whether rules are followed, respond to emergencies, or explore more than one?
risks: General concern for safety or helping people does not establish engineering interest. Separate engineering design from safety inspection and emergency care.

proposals.title: Robotics Engineers
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s is the most common response in O*NET’s new-hire education survey (50%); some respondents report associate or master’s preparation. Verify the actual role and program before fixing a route.
proposals.preparation: O*NET describes a mixed-preparation occupation rather than a universal bachelor’s-only rule; early design/test roles differ from lead systems or research roles. A robotics technician should not inherit an engineer wage or qualification claim.
interests: Integrate sensing, movement and code into robotic systems
questions: Would you like to learn to combine sensors, moving parts, and code so a robot can carry out a useful task?
Would you like to learn to test a robot, work out why it moves or responds incorrectly, and improve its design or program?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather design and program a robot, repair an existing robot, use one to make something, or none?
risks: O*NET detailed occupation nested under SOC 17-2199 Engineers, All Other; broad-SOC wages are not robotics-specific wages. Do not add both generic other-engineer and robotics as independent counts.

proposals.title: Operations Research Analysts
proposals.entry: At least bachelor’s; some employers require or prefer master’s
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Use mathematical models to compare constrained decisions
questions: Would you like to learn to use numbers and computer models to find a better delivery route, schedule, or way to use limited resources?
Would you like to learn to compare possible plans, test what happens when assumptions change, and explain the trade-offs?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather organize a plan directly, build a mathematical model to compare plans, collect customer opinions, or none?
risks: Enjoying planning or puzzles is an exploration signal, not confirmed interest in quantitative modeling. Do not require knowing the term optimization.

proposals.title: Actuaries
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in analytical field plus professional exam progression
proposals.preparation: Entry trainees commonly work while progressing through professional exams; established credentialed-practitioner wages cannot be treated as starting wages.
interests: Use probability to analyze financial uncertainty
questions: Would you like to learn to use probability and data to estimate the financial effects of uncertain events, such as accidents or illness?
Would you like to learn to test whether an insurance or pension plan can meet its future promises under different conditions?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather estimate financial risks with mathematics, advise individual customers, keep financial records, or none?
risks: A math interest alone is insufficient; confirm financial-risk application. Entry trainees and fully credentialed actuaries are different career/pay stages; many employers expect early exams.

proposals.title: Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists
proposals.entry: Typically Ph.D. in life science or medical degree; some positions have other graduate routes
proposals.preparation: Independent research may follow graduate study and temporary postdoctoral work; model the actual first-paid stage rather than assuming established researcher pay.
interests: Research mechanisms, prevention and treatment of disease
questions: Would you like to learn to design experiments that help explain why a disease develops or how a treatment could work?
Would you like to learn to compare results from medical research and test whether the evidence supports a proposed explanation?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather investigate disease through research, diagnose and treat individual patients, provide ongoing patient care, or explore several?
risks: Do not equate wanting to cure disease with physician practice. Research training, postdoctoral work, and licensed clinical responsibilities need separate route/pay descriptions.

proposals.title: Microbiologists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in microbiology or related field; some positions prefer graduate degree
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
questions: Would you like to learn to study bacteria, fungi, or other tiny living things to find out how they grow and affect people or the environment?
Would you like to learn to compare samples and experiments to identify microorganisms or test ways to control or use them?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather investigate microbes in experiments, run patient diagnostic tests, care for sick people directly, or none?
risks: Interest in science documentaries alone is weak evidence. Distinguish diagnostic service work from research; graduate independent-research opportunities are not automatic after a bachelor’s.

proposals.title: Biochemists and Biophysicists
proposals.entry: Ph.D. for independent R&D; bachelor’s/master’s qualify for some entry positions
proposals.preparation: Independent research may follow graduate study and temporary postdoctoral work; model the actual first-paid stage rather than assuming established researcher pay.
interests: Investigate chemical and physical processes in living things
questions: Would you like to learn how molecules such as proteins or DNA make cells and living things work?
Would you like to learn to plan and repeat laboratory experiments to test an explanation of a biological process?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather study how cells work, design medical equipment, provide patient care, or explore several?
risks: Do not label the independent-research role as a straightforward bachelor’s entry job. Distinguish scientific curiosity from sustained experiment-based work.

proposals.title: Forensic Science Technicians
proposals.entry: Typically bachelor’s in natural or forensic science plus on-the-job training
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
questions: Would you like to learn to examine physical evidence, such as a substance or a biological sample, to answer a specific investigation question?
Would you like to learn to document every step of an evidence test and explain what the results can and cannot show?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather analyze evidence carefully in a laboratory, interview people and investigate events, argue a legal case, or none?
risks: True-crime entertainment is not enough. Lab and scene variants differ; disturbing material and chain-of-custody are context checks, not assumptions that all work involves every exposure.

proposals.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists
proposals.entry: Typically bachelor’s in medical laboratory technology/science or related life science; licensing/certification requirements vary
proposals.preparation: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
interests: Perform and evaluate patient diagnostic laboratory tests
questions: Would you like to learn to test patient samples in a medical laboratory to help clinicians diagnose or monitor disease?
Would you like to learn to check whether a laboratory test result is accurate and investigate a result that seems wrong?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather analyze patient samples, research a new biological question, work directly with patients, or explore several?
risks: Separate bachelor-level technologist 29-2011 from associate-level technician 29-2012. The combined BLS wage reference covers both; it is not an entry wage for this exact degree route.

proposals.title: Optometrists
proposals.entry: Doctor of Optometry and state license; applicants typically have bachelor’s
proposals.preparation: Clinical entry requires the profession’s qualifying doctorate and state licensure; an undergraduate science degree alone does not qualify someone for this role. Practice ownership and specialty advancement are later stages.
interests: Diagnose and treat vision and eye-health problems
questions: Would you like to learn to examine how well someone sees and work out what is causing a vision or eye-health problem?
Would you like to learn to choose appropriate lenses or treatment and explain eye-care options to patients?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather diagnose and manage eye-health problems, design optical technology, help customers choose glasses, or none?
risks: Wearing glasses or enjoying precision gadgets is insufficient. Optometrist, ophthalmologist physician, and dispensing optician have different preparation and scopes.

proposals.title: Audiologists
proposals.entry: Doctor of Audiology after bachelor’s and state license
proposals.preparation: Clinical entry requires the profession’s qualifying doctorate and state licensure; an undergraduate science degree alone does not qualify someone for this role. Practice ownership and specialty advancement are later stages.
interests: Diagnose and manage hearing and balance problems
questions: Would you like to learn to test a person’s hearing or balance and work out what kind of problem they have?
Would you like to learn to fit and adjust hearing technology or other treatment and help someone adapt as their hearing needs change?
proposals.contrast: Would you rather diagnose hearing problems and guide treatment, teach communication skills, design audio equipment, or none?
risks: Music/audio enthusiasm is not sufficient clinical interest. Separate diagnosis and patient treatment from hearing-aid sales and sound engineering.

proposals.title: Health Education Specialists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s degree; some positions require graduate study
proposals.preparation: None in BLS typical entry classification; internships can help; Some employers require or prefer professional certification; no universal clinical-practice license inferred
questions: Would you like to learn to find out what health information a community needs and create a workshop or resource that helps people use it?
Would you like to learn to check whether a health education program is helping people and improve it from their feedback?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: teach people ways to protect their health, or provide hands-on clinical treatment to an individual patient?
risks: Adds nonclinical health-plus-teaching work, preventing every helping or prevention interest from being routed into nursing or diagnosis.

proposals.title: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s degree in occupational health/safety or related field; some jobs master’s
proposals.preparation: No universal prior-work requirement; some employers prefer industry experience; Employer-dependent certification may require education, experience and exam; distinguish specialist from technician
questions: Would you like to learn to inspect a workplace and find conditions or work habits that could injure people?
Would you like to learn to investigate why an incident happened and recommend changes that make the work safer?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: prevent injuries by changing how a workplace operates, or respond to dangerous situations once an emergency happens?
risks: Captures preventive safety investigation rather than emergency response, environmental pollution research, or production optimization.

proposals.title: Genetic Counselors
proposals.entry: Master’s in genetic counseling, normally after bachelor’s; supervised clinical rotations
proposals.preparation: Clinical training is part of preparation; do not invent independent prior employment requirement; Most states license; accredited master’s plus exam for certification; employers may require certification even where not mandated
questions: Would you like to learn how family health history and genetic test results can show a person's chance of an inherited condition?
Would you like to learn to explain genetic risks and testing choices to a worried person while supporting their own decision?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: interpret genetic information with patients and families, or investigate genes through laboratory experiments?
risks: Adds a specific science-and-counseling bridge; empathy alone or biology alone should invite exploration but cannot confirm this combined role.

proposals.title: Athletic Trainers
proposals.entry: Master’s from an accredited athletic training program
proposals.preparation: Clinical components during preparation; distinguish entry athletic trainer from head trainer; Nearly all states require licensure or certification; qualifying exam and continuing education usually apply
questions: Would you like to learn to recognize and evaluate a sports or activity injury and decide what immediate care is needed?
Would you like to learn to guide injury rehabilitation and prevention with an athlete and their health care team?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: treat and prevent activity-related injuries, or coach people mainly to improve fitness and performance?
risks: Captures clinical sports-injury interest missing between exercise physiology, emergency response and broader physical therapy; enjoying sports is insufficient.

proposals.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s entry; master’s may be needed for higher-level work; PhD commonly to lead research
proposals.preparation: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; No general license asserted; permits and field requirements depend on activity
questions: Would you like to learn to observe wildlife and record evidence about how animals behave and use their habitat?
Would you like to learn to compare animal population data and investigate how habitat changes affect survival?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: study wild animal populations and habitats, or diagnose and treat an individual animal's illness?
risks: Adds animal/ecosystem research without forcing an animal-interested student into veterinary medicine or broad land management.

proposals.title: Soil and Plant Scientists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s typical entry; specialized research may require graduate study
proposals.preparation: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; Some plant/soil work requires state licensure, supervised experience and exam; certification generally not universal
questions: Would you like to learn to compare soil, water, or growing conditions to find out why crops and other plants thrive or struggle?
Would you like to learn to test a growing method and use the results to improve plant health or crop production?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: investigate why plants grow differently through experiments, or spend most of the day planting and caring for them hands-on?
risks: Provides a college research path for growing/plant interests; farmwork interest alone should not imply experimental science, but can justify this invitation.

proposals.title: Animal Scientists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s typical BLS entry; advanced research can require master’s/PhD
proposals.preparation: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; No universal certificate asserted; distinguish this research occupation from veterinary licensure
questions: Would you like to learn to investigate how feed and living conditions affect farm animals' growth and health?
Would you like to learn to compare evidence about animal nutrition or reproduction and recommend better husbandry methods?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: investigate how groups of farm animals grow and develop, or provide medical treatment to individual animals?
risks: Adds agricultural animal biology and nutrition research, distinct from veterinary diagnosis and food-product development.

proposals.title: Hydrologists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s hydrology/geology or related field; some employers prefer master’s
proposals.preparation: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; No universal credential asserted from OOH; local practice requirements must be verified
questions: Would you like to learn to measure streams or groundwater and investigate how water moves through a place?
Would you like to learn to use rainfall and water data to estimate flood risk or future water supply?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: study how water moves and changes, or design and construct the pipes, dams, or drainage systems that control it?
risks: Adds water-cycle science, distinguishing scientific investigation from pollution generalism and infrastructure design.

proposals.title: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s in cartography, geography, geomatics or related field
proposals.preparation: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; GIS internships helpful; Licensing depends on duties/state/employer; certification usually optional
questions: Would you like to learn to turn location data and aerial images into an accurate map people can use?
Would you like to learn to compare map layers to reveal patterns such as access to services, flooding, or changes in land use?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: analyze and display geographic information, or decide the policies and development plans a community should adopt?
risks: Adds geographic analysis and mapping at the intersection of data, visual communication and environment without assuming urban-policy interest.

proposals.title: Financial Examiners
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s including accounting coursework
proposals.preparation: Entry examiners train under seniors; long-term on-job training, no prior related occupation in BLS typical classification; Professional credentials may support advancement; do not impose CPA as universal entry requirement
questions: Would you like to learn to examine a bank's records to check whether it is financially sound and following lending rules?
Would you like to learn to document a financial compliance problem and explain what needs to change?
proposals.contrast: Which would you rather learn: check whether financial institutions follow rules and protect customers, or recommend investments to improve returns?
risks: Adds regulatory/consumer financial investigation; it is not another investment-advice title or an automatic law match.

proposals.title: Financial Risk Specialists
proposals.entry: Bachelor’s typical; some employers prefer master’s

sources.title: O*NET Content Model
sources.evidence: Separates worker interests, abilities, knowledge and education from job tasks, activities and work context, and from market information. Activities form general, intermediate and detailed levels.

sources.title: O*NET May2026 Specific Interest information release
sources.evidence: May2026 introduced41specific-interest areas with occupational profiles for891data-level occupations, populated using a hybrid artificial intelligence-expert method. Treat occupational descriptors as occupational data, not student norms or a validated new Fieldguide assessment.

sources.title: Updating Vocational Interests Information for the O*NET Content Model
sources.evidence: Defines41basic-interest areas based on CABIN, with activity and occupation examples. Describes interest items as actions tied to objects/context. Medical Science, Health Care Service, Engineering and Law distinguish domains that broad helping or problem-solving can conflate.

sources.title: Su etal.,2019. Toward a dimensional model of vocational interests
sources.evidence: Develops41homogeneous basic-interest scales and an8dimension SETPOINT hierarchy. Working-adult structural and occupational-membership evidence supports measuring activity preferences below broad interest dimensions; it does not establish Fieldguide adolescent cutoffs.

sources.title: Chu etal. Interest Fit Beyond the RIASEC: CABIN-NET
sources.evidence: A60item measure of20basic-interest scales was developed in768adults and studied longitudinally in816four-year university and560community-college graduates. Authors report stronger career-outcome prediction from basic-interest fit than RIASEC fit. Transfer to younger students or our custom branching requires validation.
sources.licensingNote: Repository manuscript license is CC BY-NC-ND4.0. Do not assume unrestricted reuse/adaptation of instrument items; verify separate instrument permission. Proposed items below are original editorial drafts.

sources.title: Nye etal.,2012. Vocational Interests and Performance
sources.evidence: Across60studies and approximately568correlations, interests related to performance/persistence and person-environment congruence was more predictive than interest scores alone. Association is neither guaranteed career success nor a precise individual probability.

sources.title: Hoff etal. Adolescent vocational interests predict early career success: Two12-year longitudinal studies
sources.evidence: Two12-year samples of485and1290participants followed interests from late adolescence. Better eventual vocational fit related to later job satisfaction; interest levels and change were studied as separate predictors. This supports revisiting exploration rather than treating one profile as permanent.

sources.title: Alkan and Deniz,2023. Developing a Computerized Adaptive Test Form of the Occupational Field Interest Inventory
sources.evidence: Post-hoc CAT simulations on1425high-school students averaged59items, with correlations.91–.97between paper scores and simulated theta estimates. Efficiency depended on a calibrated item bank, model and stopping rules. It does not validate an arbitrary short decision tree.

sources.title: Kirkendall etal. Adaptive vocational interest diagnostic: Informing and improving the job assignment process
sources.evidence: Describes a military instrument combining broad/narrow interests, adaptive testing and forced choice. Useful precedent for a hierarchical architecture; civilian adolescent transfer, fake resistance and efficiency are not established for Fieldguide.

layers.detail: Preserve licensed O*NET instrument wording, administration and scoring. Store editorial domain/role probes separately; do not call their results O*NET scores or aptitude measures.

Use the41O*NET specific-interest areas as an occupational coverage checklist and a mapping aid. Introduce concrete activity probes for omitted areas such as medical research, law, engineering domains, mathematical optimization, finance and research. Use broad scores to prioritize, not permanently exclude.

Let students search any profession or select a domain. Ask what is attractive about it; a title choice starts exploration, it does not become a Top match. Allow uncertain/flat profiles to learn about work without pretending precision.

Ask about two distinct defining activities and at least one adjacent-role contrast. Use examples that do not require already knowing professional software, jargon, admissions rules or job titles. A learner should be able to imagine the activity.

Select a follow-up about the largest missing distinction, not another paraphrase of the same interest. Explain unfamiliar work neutrally, then let the student answer; keep before/after responses and whether information was shown.

After interest evidence, show training paths, licensing, academic preparation and supports, costs, time and staged pay. Distinguish interest, willingness to pursue a route and current eligibility. Keep first-paid-stage lifestyle checks and residency/prior-experience treatment.

responseDesign.interest: Five ordered anchors from strongly dislike to strongly like, with neutral/unsure; provide separate I do not yet understand this activity. Prototype choice, not validated scale.
responseDesign.exposure: Optional separate Have tried / Have observed / Have only heard of it / New to me; do not give extra interest credit for costly prior exposure.
responseDesign.selfEfficacy: Optional Can imagine learning this with support / Unsure / Want to discuss barriers. Do not mix confidence, current skill or school access into interest.
responseDesign.pairedComparisons: Use occasional adjacent-role contrasts with both/neither/unsure options; do not force students into one domain. Randomize option order in evaluation.

burdenProposal.initialDomainProbes: Prototype 8–12 short activity probes selected across underrepresented domains after the existing broad inventory, with a browse-all alternative.
burdenProposal.focusedBranch: Prototype 3–5 new questions per chosen branch, reuse genuine prior evidence, typically explore 2–3 branches and allow save/resume.
burdenProposal.qualification: These are product targets to test for completion, comprehension, accessibility and recall. They are not a psychometric minimum or a validated adaptive stopping rule. Do not call rule-based branching calibrated CAT.

scoringAndInterpretationProposal.status: Proposed evidence model, not empirical validated thresholds or likelihoods.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.independentEvidence: Track broad fit, domain interest, at least two semantically distinct defining-activity endorsements, adjacent-role differentiation, explicit contradictions and route/context information separately. Do not count the same answer multiple times because it appears in several fields or supports several occupations.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.discovery: Use weaker evidence to ask a question or offer a low-stakes work sample. Exposure eligibility should be wider than confirmed match eligibility.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.top: Require coherent occupation-specific evidence without unresolved defining-work contradictions. Compare similarly supported careers; show ties and why. Do not convert more total questions, a degree label or higher pay into stronger interest.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.negative: A clear dislike of a defining activity counts against that occupation. A dislike of an optional task, specialty or setting should branch to other variants rather than reject the whole profession. Check comprehension before treating a novice response as a firm conflict.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.unknown: Unfamiliar/unsure is missing information, not zero interest and not implicit Yes. Offer a neutral description or safe sample and ask again. Preserve status until resolved; do not impute hidden preferences from biography or demographics.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.provenance: Separate actual student choices from profile-inferred simulation answers. Inference confidence is not a psychometric probability. Show evidence excerpts and unresolved questions; original frozen histories stay immutable.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.interestVersusFeasibility: Interest evidence may justify a profession even when training feasibility is unresolved or entry pay does not sustain the lifestyle. State each separately. Financial feasibility must not create interest evidence; high salary must not be used as a rescue match.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.unvalidatedRules: Use transparent provisional rule thresholds initially and prospectively evaluate them. A copiedO*NETcorrelation threshold or twoYesrule does not acquire validity from using occupational source data.

fairnessAndLimits: Equal opportunity to learn about unfamiliar work is different from assigning equal numbers of professions. Do not use gender, ethnicity, family income or school prestige as an interest shortcut.

An adolescent without shadowing or lab access can express a coherent learning interest; lack of expensive exposure is not a disqualifier. Conversely, family exposure or a prestigious title is not sufficient evidence.
Current skill, grade history, self-efficacy, disability and financial/training barriers should be discussed as supports or feasibility, not silently treated as dislike.

RIASEC and basic-interest validity evidence is population- and instrument-specific. Fieldguide editorial questions remain exploration tools until their own validation; source-linked task accuracy alone is insufficient.

Published adult/graduate observational findings do not establish causal benefits of the proposed interface. Simulation/biography agreement tests consistency and code behavior, not student-outcome validity.

evaluationPlan.actions: Create occupation×domain×activity×route coverage matrix, mapped to SOCs and current source versions. Identify missing questions before model replays. Independent occupational experts review defining versus optional tasks and adjacent-role distinctions.

Cognitive interviews with diverse secondary students, including limited work exposure, different language backgrounds, disability/access needs and rural/low-resource contexts. Ask students to explain prompts in their own words; track jargon, leading wording and reading burden.

Keep 0.41, 0.42 and 0.44 answers and chart outputs frozen. Freeze the new question bank and offered manifest before biography-only authors answer new items. Authors must not see desired careers, outcomes or engine gates. Compare old/new status with explicit reason codes and evidence; never tune to make every model receive a degree profession.

Retain unseen holdout profiles and add counterexamples: generic helping without diagnosis; science curiosity without patient care; justice concern without legal reasoning; gadgets without medical devices; mathematics without optimization; writing without law; strong interest with low prior exposure; and clear No despite a high salary target. Check false promotions and missed plausible invitations.

Prospectively measure comprehension, completion, question burden, stability, response distributions and whether students recognize the offered work. Use independent counselor judgments and subsequent voluntary work-sample reactions as limited criteria, not agreement with the engine itself. If using a new scored scale, evaluate reliability, dimensionality, external validity and calibration before claiming a validated assessment.

Audit invited, visible, started, completed, eligible, Top, Other, pending and sustaining separately by field/route and available consented subgroup variables. Test differential item functioning/measurement comparability only with adequate data; do not infer sensitive traits from names. Evaluate whether unfamiliar responses concentrate in groups with less exposure. No numerical parity targets that force unsuitable matches.

Report unique model counts and capped visible-list counts separately, ties, evidence insufficiency and catalog absence. Track questions asked per supported offer, breadth of interest coverage, false promotion rate, missed-domain invitations and unresolved status. A higher degree Top count alone is not success.

implementationOrderProposal: Publish this audit with catalog and exposure distinctions.
Add transparent browse/search and domain discovery probes for existing overlooked professions, without changing Top thresholds automatically.
Prioritize new degree occupations by missing domains and independent source coverage, then author distinct activity questions and neutral role explanations.
Complete route/licensing/cost/first-paid-stage pay data for every new occupation before offering lifestyle coverage.
Freeze new questions, author unseen profile-consistent answers, run holdout evaluation and publish stage-by-stage chart differences with reasons.
Pilot with actual students before claiming scoring validity or calibrated adaptive efficiency.

sources.evidence: A card sort ranks 20 statements, then a formula compares them with occupational work-value ratings. Help points to the older O*NET Work Importance Locator and notes those data are no longer supported by O*NET.

sources.title: Strong 244 Technical Supplement: Items
sources.evidence: Its 244 items span five sections: occupations, subject areas, activities, people and self-described characteristics. This established assessment is not job-title-free. Some platforms randomize item order inside sections.

sources.title: Strong 244: Occupation Similarity Scales
sources.evidence: Documents 321 occupation scales. Elastic-net penalized logistic regression distinguishes occupation samples from a general reference sample using 233 holdover items; occupation-group scores have mean 50. These are interest similarity scores, not admission or career-success probabilities.

sources.title: Strong 244: Basic Interest Scales
sources.evidence: Narrower domains such as Law, Healthcare Services, Science, and Programming & Information Systems supplement broad themes. Publisher technical evidence is not automatically evidence for Fieldguide or a new adolescent population.

sources.title: YouScience Discovery FAQs,current official product description
sources.evidence: Describes game-like aptitude exercises separate from interests, with 11 exercises totaling about 90 minutes for grade 9 and beyond. Dimensions include reasoning, spatial visualization, visual comparison speed and vocabulary. Current matching is proprietary and references O*NET. Innateness and broad fairness claims are vendor claims.

sources.title: The Validity Behind YouScience, HumRRO report hosted by vendor
sources.evidence: An older report describes an augmented Ball Aptitude Battery, 60-item O*NET interests, expert mappings to O*NET descriptors, comparable scaling, profile similarity and simulated-user vetting. Full operational weights are not provided. Its older battery description differs from the current FAQ, so version equivalence is unverified.

sources.title: Morrisby Profile Administration Guide, updated August 11, 2026
sources.evidence: At age 15 and beyond, students complete verbal, numerical, abstract, spatial and mechanical tasks plus interests/personality questionnaires; optional priorities and study interests follow. Full configuration takes about 1 hour 50 minutes. Performance and self-report modules are distinct.

sources.title: Morrisby Profile: official product page
sources.evidence: Says abilities, interests and personality inform career/subject recommendations and later exploration. Statements about independence from educational or social background are vendor claims, not independently established fairness conclusions in this review.

sources.title: Morrisby history
sources.evidence: Describes a fuzzy-logic expert system begun in the 1970s and still used. This does not reveal current weights, calibration or a reproducible matching specification.

sources.title: Kuder Navigator assessment instructions, August 11, 2026
sources.evidence: Interest questions ask how much activities are liked/disliked. Skills Confidence separately asks confidence in performing tasks, explicitly not liking. Work Values ranks priorities. Confidence is self-perceived ability, not an objective performance test.

sources.title: KCIA-L Technical Brief, August 1, 2019
sources.evidence: The 60-item KCIA-L measures six Holland interest areas. O*NET occupations are matched by Euclidean distance; pathway/cluster profiles use constituent-occupation medians. Reports student think-alouds, item analysis, structural validity and DIF checks. Historical evidence does not prove current combined-platform outcomes.

sources.title: How to Utilize Kuder Navigator, August 11, 2026
sources.evidence: Current help describes grades 6–12, separate repeatable assessments and more than 1,000 occupations organized by results, clusters/pathways or title. Career pages then explain pay, education and tasks.

establishedSystems.name: O*NET / My Next Move

establishedSystems.roleCues: Users need not nominate a profession, but many activities are recognizably related to occupations. The method does not claim complete freedom from preconceptions.
establishedSystems.learnMore: Results lead to occupational tasks, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, pay and outlook.
establishedSystems.evidence: Public technical manual and occupational mappings; comparatively inspectable.
establishedSystems.cannotInfer: No aptitude, admissions probability or guaranteed earnings. Custom rewording or shortening does not inherit official validity.

establishedSystems.name: CareerOneStop

establishedSystems.roleCues: Activities, skill statements and values allow discovery beyond a named profession. Self-ratings still depend on experience, awareness and confidence.
establishedSystems.learnMore: Profiles expose education, training, occupational attributes and national/state labor data.
establishedSystems.evidence: Official public tools and API description; formula disclosure varies by tool.
establishedSystems.cannotInfer: Self-rating is not demonstrated ability or learning potential. Do not silently average these constructs into an aptitude percentage.

establishedSystems.name: Strong 244
establishedSystems.matchingMechanism: Occupational similarity models are learned from occupation versus reference-group responses. A wider pattern can suggest a profession without endorsement of its title.
establishedSystems.roleCues: Includes named occupations alongside other item types. It does not establish that masking all career terms is necessary or sufficient.
establishedSystems.learnMore: Occupation and academic-major similarity scales support interpretation and exploration.
establishedSystems.evidence: Current publisher supplement documents items, scales and modeling; distinguish it from independent prospective adolescent outcomes.
establishedSystems.cannotInfer: Cannot copy proprietary items or train a comparable empirical classifier on 154 fictional models. Similarity is not a calibrated success probability.

establishedSystems.name: YouScience
establishedSystems.matchingMechanism: Current matching is proprietary. An older HumRRO report describes expert mappings to O*NET descriptors, comparable scaling, similarity and simulated-profile testing.
establishedSystems.roleCues: Reasoning and spatial exercises do not require career choices and can yield a different list from self-reported interests. That does not eliminate test, exposure or accessibility effects.
establishedSystems.learnMore: Current FAQ describes career possibilities and educational pathways after assessment.
establishedSystems.evidence: Current product FAQ plus an older vendor-hosted technical report; current-version mapping and coefficients remain unverified.
establishedSystems.cannotInfer: Do not repeat hard-wired or universal fairness promises as fact. Homemade puzzles, biography interpretation and self-reported strengths are not equivalent aptitude testing.

revisedFieldguideArchitecture.designProposal: Keep the official broad interest inventory unchanged. New editorial discovery should ask about varied activities, questions and ways of working in familiar contexts, without first displaying career names, pay, degrees or prestige. Sample several contexts for each construct.
originalExamplePrototypes: Compare two explanations and look for evidence that would tell them apart.
Work out a fair solution when people have conflicting needs and a shared rule.
Build a small model, test it, and change one feature to see what improves.
Look for a pattern in observations, then explain what might make it misleading.
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.limitation: These are unvalidated examples. Abstract verbs alone cannot distinguish professions; everyday contexts also carry culture and exposure. Test comprehension and bias.

revisedFieldguideArchitecture.designProposal: Optional self-reported strengths should use concrete examples and evidence from familiar activities. Record learning confidence and exposure separately. Objective aptitude requires an appropriately licensed, validated performance battery, age norms and accommodations.
examples: Interest: I would enjoy figuring out why the results disagree.
Confidence: I feel able to explain my reasoning clearly today.
Exposure: I have tried this / observed it / it is new to me.
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.limitation: Grades, hobbies, self-ratings and biographies are context, not direct estimates of innate ability or professional readiness.

revisedFieldguideArchitecture.stage: 3. Generate a wide range of possibilities
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.designProposal: Retrieve from the entire source-backed catalog using full interest patterns and several independent clues. Do not restrict discovery to the first three fields or require confirmed role interest before introducing unfamiliar work. Offer cross-field and degree-route possibilities with their evidence limits.
examples: Evidence comparison plus biological curiosity can invite health research or clinical-reasoning exploration.
Rules and fairness plus careful argument can invite legal, policy, compliance or social-research exploration.
Model testing plus spatial and systems curiosity can invite engineering, design or technical-science exploration.
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.limitation: These are invitations or initial interest possibilities. Generic helping is not physician evidence; talking is not lawyer evidence; liking mathematics is not sufficient engineering evidence.

revisedFieldguideArchitecture.stage: 4. Reveal and learn about the work
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.designProposal: After initial retrieval, reveal professions through plain-language explanations, neutral day-in-the-life examples and adjacent-role comparisons. Show why each appeared and what remains unknown. Students may save, pass or learn more. Realistic work functions matter at this later stage.
examples: Medicine: individual diagnosis/treatment versus disease research versus population health.
Law: legal research/advice/documents versus courtroom advocacy versus policy analysis.
Engineering: design/test versus build/install/repair versus investigate underlying science.
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.limitation: Avoid leading questions such as whether someone wants to be a doctor. Record which explanation was shown and distinguish responses before and after exposure.

revisedFieldguideArchitecture.designProposal: Offer brief, accessible, safe work examples and ask which parts were interesting, tedious or worth learning. Score performance as aptitude only when the activity has appropriate validation; otherwise label it experiential exploration.
examples: Compare brief arguments and identify missing evidence.
Change a design-model parameter and observe a tradeoff.
Read a simple pattern display and propose an alternative explanation.
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.limitation: A brief sample is not professional competency. Offer accessible alternatives; unfamiliar formats or speed should not exclude a whole domain.

revisedFieldguideArchitecture.stage: 6. Keep fit, confirmation, route and money distinct
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.designProposal: Display initial possibilities, supported matches, unresolved work questions and student choices as separate states. Preserve current Top meaning until a versioned change is evaluated; a broad pattern result may instead be labeled an interest match with confirmation recorded separately. Show route willingness, preparation and financial feasibility separately.
revisedFieldguideArchitecture.limitation: Salary, prestige, parent preferences and willingness to study do not create work interest. A realistic non-sustaining match is preferable to a forced high-pay near-match.

specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.earlierPrompts: Direct physician, lawyer and engineer prompts in question-method-research.json belong in later realistic exploration, not the primary discovery bank. First infer relevant areas from multiple activities and constructs, then reveal and investigate roles.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.discoveryVsConfirmation: Do not require two Yes answers about named job functions before a profession can appear as an initial interest possibility. Do not automatically call an unknown specialty a fully confirmed Top match either. Make the stage and uncertainty visible.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.catalogScale: Expand by source-backed SOC domains. Require occupational identity, interest attributes, defining activities and sources before discovery publication. Route, licensing, prior experience, first-paid-stage pay and budget evidence are additionally needed for lifestyle coverage. Missing feasibility data should be visible, never fabricated.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.scalableMapping: Map new editorial discovery questions to explicit constructs first, then map constructs to occupation attributes. This scales better than only hand-written career-ID lists. Keep an inspectable translation table, provenance and independent review; custom scores remain provisional until validated.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.sharedEvidence: Multiple careers may share activity evidence. Count distinct constructs rather than paraphrases or raw mapped-item totals. Ask another differentiator only when it would change guidance.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.negativeEvidence: Keep dislike, unfamiliar, uncertain, no exposure and not selected separate. Unknown is neither No nor Yes. Disliking an optional variant is not rejection of the entire profession; an informed dislike of defining work is a material contradiction.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.wholeProfile: Use all six interest scores, not one highest letter or hobby. Flat profiles should allow open discovery with uncertainty. Broad correlations alone cannot distinguish every specialty.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.fairness: Title masking is not proof of bias removal. Test reading, culture, accessibility, ordering and title/pay-visibility effects with real students. Avoid demographic assumptions and requirements for expensive shadowing.
specificRevisionsToEarlierRecommendation.frozenModels: The 154 profiles are a regression and consistency set, not occupation-classifier training data, student norms or outcome validation. Freeze new questions and biography-based answers before replay; preserve all prior rounds.

evaluationPlan: Pilot activity-only discovery against career-labeled prompts with randomized order and no early pay/degree cues. Measure comprehension, unfamiliar responses and new possibilities considered. More college suggestions alone does not prove lower bias.
Have independent occupational experts and counselors review construct mappings and adjacent-role coverage before seeing desired matching outcomes.

Use unseen holdouts and counterexamples: helping without clinical reasoning, mathematics without design, debate without legal research. Preserve plausible unknowns for learning and reject forced promotions.

Pilot with real students for completion, accessibility, response stability and recognition of actual work after neutral previews. If creating scales, evaluate their content, structure and external evidence. Simulation is not external validation.

Chart catalogued, retrieved, invited, visible, opened, answered, supported, Top, Other, pending, chosen and sustaining stages separately. Distinguish unique occupation counts from capped displayed lists.
Preserve original profiles, initial candidates, exposure records, new answers, final matches, choices and budgets as versioned stages. Show actual versus inferred provenance and why results changed.
established.implementationRecommendation: Expand catalog and discovery retrieval within verified source coverage. Stage the broader activity/construct layer separately from the existing official inventory, preserving historical matches. Introduce unfamiliar careers where evidence justifies learning; promote only with coherent work evidence, without degree or pay quotas.

proposalsPurpose: 41 priority profiles for deeper preparation/pay/planning review within the systematic expanded inventory, not the total size of the expansion.
